name: Additive-Combinatorics Density Dichotomy for Subset Sum (sumsets, additive energy, Kneser/AP structure)
description: A line of work that solves Subset Sum in near-linear time on dense instances by exploiting additive structure of sumsets. Bringmann-Wellnitz (SODA 2021) revived and improved Galil-Margalit (SICOMP 1991): if the target t is large relative to the item sizes (roughly t >> a_max * Sigma_X / n^2), then dense Subset Sum is solvable in near-linear time OTilde(n) for the decision problem, using sparse convolution plus sumset estimates and an adaptation of Sarkozy's addition theorem. Chen-Mao-Zhang (STOC 2025) then gave constructive proofs of Sarkozy's finite addition theorems, yielding an OTilde(n)-time algorithm that actually returns a long arithmetic progression inside the sumset plus, for each term, an explicit representation as a sum of input elements; this upgrades dense Subset Sum and Unbounded Subset Sum from decision to search. The same additive-combinatorics toolkit (Kneser's theorem for n-fold Boolean convolution, sumset/additive-energy/doubling structure) also underlies the pseudopolynomial algorithm OTilde(n + sqrt(a_max t)) of Chen-Lian-Mao-Zhang (FOCS 2024). The dichotomy is: dense instances are easy (near-linear, poly space) and sparse (density ~ 1, random-knapsack-like) instances have no long progressions and are not touched, so this line does not improve the general O*(2^{n/2}) worst-case bound.
worst_case_time: On dense / large-target instances: OTilde(n) time (near-linear) for the decision problem (Bringmann-Wellnitz, SODA 2021) and now for the search problem (Chen-Mao-Zhang, STOC 2025); Unbounded Subset Sum solvable in O(n log a_max) for all t >= c * a_max^2 / n. On general instances (arbitrary density) this approach gives no sub-2^{n/2} bound; the state of the art remains O*(2^{n/2}) (Horowitz-Sahni meet-in-the-middle). Pseudopolynomial cousin: OTilde(n + sqrt(a_max * t)) for the decision problem (Chen-Lian-Mao-Zhang, FOCS 2024).
space_complexity: Near-linear / polynomial space for the dense algorithms (the constructive AP search is reported to run in O(n log a_max) time and polynomial space) [uncertain] exact space bound not stated in the abstract.
model: Word RAM (unit-cost logarithmically-bounded word RAM); randomized/sorting-based primitives over integers. [uncertain] whether all routines are word-RAM or plain RAM.
randomized_or_deterministic: The Chen-Mao-Zhang constructive addition-theorem/search algorithm is deterministic; Bringmann-Wellnitz's original dense algorithm is randomized [uncertain] (Monte Carlo-style numerics).
numerical_exponent_and_record_year: Dense regime: base-2 exponent 0 (linear up to polylog), records 2021 (decision) and 2025 (search/witness). General worst-case: unchanged exponent 1/2 (i.e. 2^{n/2}); this line contributes no constant c > 0 for 2^{(1/2-c)n}.
problem_variant: Dense Subset Sum (large target / polynomial-size items); Unbounded Subset Sum; decision and search versions; related to bounded-integer convolution and n-fold Boolean convolution.
applies_to: Positive-integer Subset Sum instances in the dense regime, i.e. item sizes and target bounded by poly(n) or with t >> a_max * Sigma_X / n^2; Unbounded Subset Sum for t >= c * a_max^2 / n. Does not apply to sparse, low-density, or random-knapsack-style instances ({0,1} subset sum at density ~ 1).
coefficient_set: {0,1} for vanilla Subset Sum; {0,1,2,...} (unbounded multiplicities) for Unbounded Subset Sum; general bounded integer coefficients in the convolution formulations.
density_regime: High density / dense: d = n / log2(max|a_i|) large (items and target polynomial in n), equivalently t >> a_max * Sigma_X / n^2. The complementary low-density regime (d ~ 1 or less, e.g. cryptographic knapsacks) is explicitly outside the reach of this method.
solution_regime: General decision, extended by Chen-Mao-Zhang (STOC 2025) to the search/witness version for dense instances; not a promised/numerous-solution (pigeonhole) regime.
cardinality_constraint: No fixed-cardinality constraint; solutions may use any number of items.
key_technique: Additive combinatorics of sumsets: long arithmetic progressions in subset sums (Sarkozy's finite addition theorems), sumset size / Freiman-type structure, small doubling and additive energy, and Kneser's theorem (used centrally for n-fold Boolean and bounded-integer convolution, Bringmann-Nakos ICALP 2021). Algorithmically: sparse convolution, sumset estimates, and constructive/recursive recovery of progressions and their representations.
core_idea: In dense instances the subset-sumset necessarily contains a long arithmetic progression with a small step and small start; one finds such a progression (now constructively) and, because every term has a representation using few base elements, recovers an explicit witness. This replaces exponential enumeration over subset sums by near-linear-time sumset manipulation, which is why the dense case collapses to OTilde(n). Sparse instances have no long progressions in their sumsets, so the technique gives nothing there and cannot touch the 2^{n/2} worst case.
reduction_pipeline: Subset Sum -> sumset S(A) and its additive structure (long AP with small step) -> recover representation per AP term; convolution route: Subset Sum/knapsack counting -> n-fold Boolean / bounded-integer convolution solved via Kneser's theorem and additive structure. Chen-Lian-Mao-Zhang use Szemeredi-Vu for arithmetic progressions in the pseudopolynomial route.
constructive_vs_existential: Constructive. The key novelty of Chen-Mao-Zhang (STOC 2025) is turning the previously existential Sárközy addition theorems into constructive proofs that output the AP and explicit element-set representations, closing the decision-vs-search gap for dense Subset Sum.
search_vs_decision_witness: Returns an explicit witness for dense Subset Sum (each AP term's representation as a sum of base elements); prior additive-combinatorics algorithms handled only decision.
obstacle_to_2n3: The method is confined to the dense regime and gives near-linear time there, not an exponential-base saving on general instances. Sparse / low-density instances (density ~ 1, random knapsack) have sumsets with no long arithmetic progressions, so the additive structural hypothesis is vacuous; reaching O*(2^{n/3}) on general ({0,1}) Subset Sum would require handling instances where this toolkit provably does not apply. Moreover the near-linear guarantee requires t polynomially large relative to a_max * Sigma / n^2; below that threshold the method fails and a conditional lower bound rules out near-linear time.
potential_to_break_mitm: low for the general worst-case MITM barrier (it solves only the complementary dense regime, not sparse hard instances); medium-to-high only for the dense subproblem, where it already beats 2^{n/2} by an exponential margin.
barrier_evidence: Bringmann-Wellnitz prove a conditional lower bound: a subquadratic or near-linear algorithm for the regime t << a_max * Sigma_X / n^2 would contradict SETH and the Strong k-SUM Hypothesis, so the dense algorithm's threshold is essentially tight. The method's applicability condition is also a barrier: additive structure (long progressions in the sumset) simply fails for sparse/random instances, so the approach is structurally incapable of handling them.
open_questions: Can constructive addition theorems be extended to less dense / multi-dimensional settings with matching bounds (multi-dimensional dense subset sum)? Can the dense decision-vs-search gap be closed under weaker target conditions or for multisets where upper and lower bounds do not match? Can Kneser-theorem-style convolution methods be combined with worst-case representation/mixing techniques to attack sparse instances? Is there a deterministic near-linear search algorithm under minimal target assumptions?
conditional_hypothesis: SETH and the Strong k-SUM Hypothesis underlie the matching conditional lower bound at the density threshold; Kneser's theorem and Sarkozy/Szemeredi-Vu addition theorems are unconditional additive-combinatorics ingredients (no hardness assumption for the positive dense result).
worst_case_vs_average_case_guarantee: Worst-case within the restricted dense regime (guarantee conditional on t >> a_max * Sigma_X / n^2), and constructive. Not a general worst-case guarantee; it deliberately excludes the hard, sparse, worst-case instances.
cryptographic_regime: Orthogonal/complementary to low-density knapsack cryptanalysis (Lagarias-Odlyzko, density d < 0.94): those attacks live in exactly the sparse regime this line cannot handle. Relevance is the density dichotomy itself, sharpening where dense methods stop and lattice/representation methods take over; no attack on cryptographic knapsacks.
pseudopolynomial_interaction: Strong. The line is intertwined with pseudopolynomial algorithms: Chen-Lian-Mao-Zhang (FOCS 2024) give OTilde(n + sqrt(a_max t)) time for decision Subset Sum using the dense-or-sparse framework and Szemeredi-Vu, and the dense algorithms merge with DP/proximity to handle small-item regimes.

empirical_evidence: None found: this is a theory line; no benchmark tables or experiments reported in the primary papers [uncertain].
verification_method: Verify the constructive addition-theorem proofs line by line; check the dense-to-Subset-Sum reduction and the explicit representation extraction; reproduce the conditional lower bound reduction from SETH / Strong k-SUM; implement the near-linear progression search and test on dense random instances (items/target poly(n)) and boundary cases near t = a_max * Sigma_X / n^2.
